title: First Light
speaker: nova
line: Commander, we have enough energy to start only a few systems. Which ones come first?
context: The solar panels are working, but the batteries don't have enough power for everything.

choices.label: Save power for later
choices.result: The base stays dim and chilly, but the battery strips glow brighter.

choices.label: Use power for heating
choices.result: Warm light fills the habitat windows as the heaters hum on.

choices.label: Use power for communication
choices.result: The antenna light blinks as the crew's first message heads to Earth.

why.text: NASA's Moon base plans use solar arrays, plus other power sources for the long lunar night.

title: Long Shadows
speaker: rex
line: Commander, the Sun is sliding behind the ridge. Our panels will be in shadow soon.
context: Near the south pole the Sun stays low, so shadows sweep across the panels. Plan your power before dark.

choices.label: Tilt panels toward the Sun
choices.result: The panels swing slowly to catch the last light on the ridge.

choices.label: Charge the batteries now
choices.result: The battery strips glow full while the habitat lights dim.

choices.label: Switch off the lab
choices.result: The lab and the greenhouse go dark to save every watt.

why.text: Near the Moon's south pole, the Sun stays low in the sky. Some ridges get sunlight most of the time, and some craters never see sunlight.

title: Breathing Room
speaker: nova
line: Commander, our life-support system is using more power than expected.
context: The crew needs breathable air, but the base also needs electricity for other equipment.

choices.label: Run air machines on full
choices.result: The air machines roar at full speed, and the battery strips dim.

choices.label: Turn air machines down
choices.result: The air machines slow to a quiet hum, and the air feels stuffy.

choices.label: Shut off heaters & science lab
choices.benefit: Oxygen +10 (power goes to the air machines)
choices.result: The heaters and lab screens click off, and the air machines keep running.

why.text: NASA uses life-support systems to provide oxygen, remove carbon dioxide, and maintain safe air inside spacecraft.

title: Filter Change
speaker: nova
line: The carbon dioxide filter is clogging up. The air is getting stale.
context: Life support must remove the carbon dioxide the crew breathes out. A clogged filter needs fixing.

choices.label: Replace the filter
choices.result: A fresh filter clicks into place and the air clears.

choices.label: Clean and reuse it
choices.result: The crew scrubs the old filter carefully and slots it back in.

choices.label: Run the backup scrubber
choices.result: A second machine hums to life beside the first.

why.text: Life-support systems aboard the International Space Station provide oxygen, remove carbon dioxide, and recycle water.

title: The Green Room
speaker: luna
line: Our first crops are growing, but they need water, energy, and time.
context: The crew wants to grow food, but plants need water, light, and time.

choices.label: Grow more plants
choices.risk: Water and electricity may run low.
choices.result: Tiny seedlings fill every tray under the bright grow lights.

choices.label: Grow fewer plants
choices.benefit: Food +10 next sol, and it saves resources
choices.result: A few neat rows of plants grow, using less water and power.

choices.label: Reduce the lighting time
choices.result: The greenhouse lights dim, and the little plants grow more slowly.

why.text: NASA has grown vegetables aboard the International Space Station using LED lights, water, and nutrients.

title: Thirsty Plants
speaker: luna
line: The water recycler is running slow, and the plants are thirsty.
context: On a base, water is recycled again and again. It is used for drinking, making oxygen and growing plants.

choices.label: Repair the recycler
choices.result: The recycler gurgles back to full speed.

choices.label: Ration drinking water
choices.result: Everyone gets a smaller cup today.

choices.label: Water the plants less
choices.result: The leaves droop a little as the sprinklers slow down.

why.text: Water on a base is recycled. It is used for drinking, for oxygen-making systems and for plants.

title: Dust on the Panels
speaker: rex
line: Commander, the dust is blocking sunlight. Our batteries aren't charging fast enough.
context: Moon dust has collected on the solar panels, reducing the amount of electricity they produce.

choices.label: Use a cleaning robot
choices.result: BOLT rolls out and sweeps the grey dust off the panels.

choices.label: Send an astronaut to clean
choices.risk: The astronaut needs extra equipment and protection.
choices.result: An astronaut suits up and carefully brushes every panel clean.

choices.label: Wait and save electricity
choices.risk: The dusty panels continue producing less power.
choices.result: The panels stay grey with dust while the base saves every watt.

why.text: NASA tested a dust shield on the Moon that pushed dust off glass and radiator surfaces. Solar panels could use it next.

title: Dusty Airlock
speaker: rex
line: Commander, we tracked Moon dust inside. It sticks to everything.
context: Moon dust clings to suits and tools. Inside the base, it gets into machines and the air.

choices.label: Clean suits before entering
choices.result: The crew brushes every suit down in the airlock.

choices.label: Vacuum the airlock
choices.result: A loud vacuum sucks the grey dust out of the airlock.

choices.label: Skip the cleaning today
choices.result: A thin grey film settles on the habitat floor.

why.text: Lunar dust can stick to equipment and reduce the performance of solar panels.

title: Radiation Shelter
speaker: nova
line: Commander, high-energy particles from the Sun may reach our base. The crew needs extra protection.
context: A solar storm is approaching the Moon. The crew moves into the shelter whatever you choose. You decide how to prepare it.

choices.label: Add water shielding
choices.result: Water containers line the shelter walls like a thick blanket.

choices.label: Move extra supplies inside
choices.benefit: Radiation dose −10 now, −10 next sol (the crew can stay inside longer)
choices.result: Boxes of food and supplies are stacked safely inside the shelter.

choices.label: Shut down research equipment
choices.benefit: Power +15 for the shelter, Radiation dose −10
choices.result: The research lab goes dark, and the shelter lights glow brighter.

why.text: Solar storms can send high-energy particles toward the Moon. NASA studies protective shelters and materials such as water and stored supplies to help shield astronauts.

title: Spacewalk Abort
speaker: nova
line: Two crew members are still outside fixing a panel. The storm is close.
context: Spacewalks are planned around safety. When danger comes, crews stop and come back inside.

choices.label: Bring them in now
choices.result: The airlock door shuts behind the two returning astronauts.

choices.label: Finish the repair fast
choices.result: The panel lights up just as the crew rushes back inside.

choices.label: Send BOLT to finish
choices.result: BOLT rolls out alone and tightens the last bolts.

why.text: The Moon has no global magnetic field and no thick atmosphere, so solar particles reach the surface. Shelter and mass, like soil or water, help block radiation.

title: Final Emergency Decision
speaker: nova
line: Commander, we need your decision. The crew is counting on you.
context: The solar storm has arrived. The Moon base's batteries are running low after earlier power problems.

choices.label: Turn off extra gadgets
choices.benefit: Life Support +15 (the saved power goes to it)
choices.result: Screens and gadgets click off, and the air machines keep humming.

choices.label: Use backup batteries
choices.result: The backup batteries click on, and the emergency lights steady.

choices.label: Send an emergency message
choices.risk: Less electricity remains for the base.
choices.result: The antenna flickers as an emergency message races toward Earth.

why.text: Solar storms can affect spacecraft electronics and communications. Backup power systems help keep important equipment running. In this game, the blackout happens mainly because the base has already used most of its stored electricity.

title: Radio Silence
speaker: nova
line: The storm has cut our link to Earth. We have to decide on our own.
context: Earth is usually only seconds away by radio, but storms and the horizon can block the signal.

choices.label: Follow the emergency checklist
choices.result: The crew works through the checklist, one step at a time.

choices.label: Keep calling Earth
choices.result: The antenna light keeps blinking into the static.

choices.label: Rest and wait it out
choices.result: The crew sleeps in shifts while the storm passes overhead.

why.text: Radio signals take about 1.3 seconds to travel between Earth and the Moon.

title: First Light
speaker: aster
line: Commander, we have enough energy to start only a few systems. Which ones come first?
context: The batteries don't have enough power for everything. The crew needs electricity for lighting, heating, and essential equipment.

choices.label: Save power for later
choices.result: The base stays dim and chilly, but the battery strips glow brighter.

choices.label: Use power for heating
choices.result: Warm light fills the habitat windows as the heaters hum on.

choices.label: Use power for communication
choices.result: The antenna light blinks as the crew's first message heads home.

why.text: Solar-powered spacecraft on Mars collect sunlight to generate electricity. Batteries store energy for times when sunlight is unavailable.

title: Breathing Room
speaker: aster
line: Commander, our life-support system is using more power than expected.
context: Machines make oxygen and remove carbon dioxide. They need electricity, and the base is still short on power.

choices.label: Keep life support running normally
choices.result: The oxygen generator keeps humming and the air stays fresh.

choices.label: Turn off unnecessary equipment
choices.result: Spare lights and screens click off all around the base.

choices.label: Delay nonessential research
choices.result: The science desks go quiet, and the batteries start to fill.

why.text: Life-support systems aboard the International Space Station provide oxygen, remove carbon dioxide, and recycle water.

title: The Green Room
speaker: zara
line: Our first crops are growing, but they need water, energy, and time.
context: Plants need water, light, and time to grow. The greenhouse uses resources needed elsewhere.

choices.label: Grow more plants
choices.result: Tiny seedlings fill every tray under the bright grow lights.

choices.label: Grow fewer plants
choices.result: A few neat rows of plants grow, using less water and power.

choices.label: Reduce the lighting time
choices.result: The greenhouse lights dim, and the little plants grow more slowly.

why.text: Astronauts have successfully grown lettuce and other plants aboard the International Space Station using special lighting, water, and nutrients.

title: Dust on the Panels
speaker: alex
line: Commander, the dust is blocking sunlight. Our batteries aren't charging fast enough.
context: Red dust is blocking sunlight on the solar panels. Cleaning them takes time and resources.

choices.label: Use the cleaning robot
choices.result: The cleaning robot rolls out and sweeps red dust off the panels.

choices.label: Send a trained crew member
choices.result: A crew member suits up and carefully brushes the panels clean.

choices.label: Save power for now
choices.result: The panels stay red with dust while the base saves every watt.

why.text: NASA's InSight lander experienced major power losses as dust accumulated on its solar panels. Its daily energy production dropped from about 5,000 to 500 watt-hours by 2022.

title: Radiation Shelter
speaker: aster
line: Commander, high-energy particles from the Sun may reach our base. The crew needs extra protection.
context: Mars has no global magnetic field. The shelter protects the crew, but preparing it takes electricity and supplies.

choices.label: Move into the shelter
choices.result: The crew moves into the shelter, and its door light glows.

choices.label: Shield with water containers
choices.result: Water containers line the shelter walls like a thick blanket.

choices.label: Move supplies to the shelter
choices.result: Boxes of food and spare parts are stacked safely in the shelter.

why.text: On May 20, 2024, NASA's Curiosity rover recorded its largest radiation surge since landing on Mars in 2012. This provides real evidence of the danger solar storms could pose to future astronauts.

title: Final Emergency Decision
speaker: aster
line: Commander, we need your decision. The crew is counting on you.
context: The storm has arrived. Oxygen, shelter equipment, and communications all need power, and there isn't enough for everything.

choices.label: Give priority to life support
choices.result: Every spare watt flows to the air and water machines.

choices.label: Switch to backup batteries
choices.result: The backup batteries click on and the emergency lights steady.

choices.label: Send an emergency message
choices.result: The antenna flickers as an emergency message races toward Earth.

why.text: Space radiation is a major challenge for future human Mars missions. Solar storms can also interfere with spacecraft electronics and communications. The power shortage in this story is caused by the base's earlier energy problems.

title: The Water Search
speaker: luna
line: Searching for ice takes time, electricity, and equipment.
context: The Moon base needs more water. Scientists believe frozen water may exist inside some very cold craters near the Moon's poles.

choices.label: Send a rover to search
choices.risk: The rover may not find usable ice.
choices.result: The rover rolls out and maps possible ice locations.

choices.label: Search a nearby crater
choices.risk: The crater may contain little or no ice.
choices.result: The crew investigates a possible water source in the crater.

choices.label: Save the stored water
choices.result: The crew cuts water use while they wait for more information.

why.text: NASA has confirmed water ice in permanently shadowed regions of the Moon. Scientists are studying whether this ice could support future astronauts.

title: Rover Trouble
speaker: rex
line: The rover may become stuck or damaged if it continues along the same route.
context: A rover is exploring the Moon when it reaches an area with loose soil and large rocks.

choices.label: Keep driving forward
choices.risk: Its wheels may lose traction or become stuck.
choices.result: The rover attempts to cross the difficult area.

choices.label: Find another route
choices.benefit: Morale +10 (the rover avoids the rough ground)
choices.result: The rover turns away and avoids the difficult terrain.

choices.label: Send another rover
choices.risk: More equipment and electricity are used.
choices.result: A second rover rolls out to help with the mission.

why.text: NASA develops and tests lunar rover wheels and navigation systems to help vehicles travel across rough, dusty terrain.

title: The Shadow Problem
speaker: rex
line: The panels cannot collect enough sunlight while they remain in shadow.
context: The base is near the Moon's south pole. A nearby hill casts a long shadow over part of the solar panel area.

choices.label: Move panels into sunlight
choices.benefit: Solar input +20 (more sunlight reaches the panels)
choices.risk: Moving equipment takes time and resources.
choices.result: The crew carries the panels out of the shadow.

choices.label: Raise the solar panels
choices.risk: The raised structure needs extra support.
choices.result: The panels rise on tall posts above the shadow.

choices.label: Keep panels where they are
choices.risk: The panels continue collecting less energy.
choices.result: The panels stay put, half in shadow.

why.text: Near the Moon's south pole, the Sun stays close to the horizon. Hills and craters can create very long shadows that affect solar power.

title: Lost Signal
speaker: rex
line: Important information needs to reach Earth, but the connection is unreliable.
context: The Moon base is having trouble communicating with Earth. The surrounding terrain is blocking part of the signal.

choices.label: Adjust the antenna
choices.risk: The signal may still be blocked.
choices.result: The antenna turns slowly toward a clear direction.

choices.label: Save messages for later
choices.result: Important data is stored until communication improves.

choices.label: Use more transmission power
choices.risk: Extra power cannot solve every signal blockage.
choices.result: The antenna light glows brighter as it transmits harder.

why.text: Near the lunar south pole, Earth can appear very low on the horizon or become hidden by the terrain. This makes direct communication difficult.

title: Spacesuit Check
speaker: nova
line: The spacesuit must be checked before the astronaut can leave safely.
context: An astronaut is preparing to explore outside the base. A spacesuit inspection shows that some equipment needs attention.

choices.label: Replace worn equipment
choices.result: The crew swaps the worn part for a new one.

choices.label: Refill suit supplies
choices.risk: The original equipment problem still needs checking.
choices.result: The suit's supplies are topped up.

choices.label: Delay the exploration
choices.benefit: Health +10 (more time to inspect the suit)
choices.result: The suit stays on its rack for a careful check.

why.text: Spacesuits contain equipment for temperature control and communication. Astronauts need these systems when exploring outside a spacecraft.

title: Crew Fitness
speaker: nova
line: The astronauts must stay physically fit while also completing their missions.
context: After several days of work, the crew needs time for exercise and recovery.

choices.label: Complete an exercise session
choices.result: The crew trains hard in the habitat gym.

choices.label: Take shorter exercise sessions
choices.risk: It may not be enough if repeated too often.
choices.result: The crew fits in a short workout between tasks.

choices.label: Delay exercise
choices.risk: Missing exercise regularly may affect fitness.
choices.result: The crew skips the gym and heads to the lab.

why.text: Astronauts exercise regularly in space to help protect their muscles and bones. The Moon has about one-sixth of Earth's gravity, and scientists are studying how reduced gravity affects astronaut health.

title: The Cold Zone
speaker: rex
line: Extreme cold can damage equipment and reduce its performance.
context: A scientific instrument has been left outside in a very cold, shadowed area.

choices.label: Use an equipment heater
choices.result: A small heater glows beside the instrument.

choices.label: Move equipment indoors
choices.result: The crew carries the instrument inside the base.

choices.label: Switch off the instrument
choices.risk: It may still become too cold without protection.
choices.result: The instrument goes dark and quiet.

why.text: Temperatures on the Moon can become extremely low during darkness. NASA has used special heaters to protect scientific instruments on the lunar surface.

title: Moonquake Alert
speaker: nova
line: The crew needs to check whether the vibrations have affected the base.
context: Sensors inside the base detect small vibrations coming from the ground.

choices.label: Check the base sensors
choices.result: The sensor screens light up one by one.

choices.label: Stop research and inspect
choices.benefit: Morale +10 (more time to check the base)
choices.result: The crew walks the base, checking every wall.

choices.label: Continue normal activities
choices.result: Work carries on as the ground settles.

why.text: Apollo astronauts placed instruments on the Moon that detected moonquakes. Some moonquakes are caused by the Moon shrinking as it cools.

title: Small Impacts
speaker: rex
line: Small space rocks can strike the Moon because it has almost no atmosphere to stop them.
context: Cameras detect a new impact mark near some equipment outside the Moon base.

choices.label: Inspect using cameras
choices.risk: Cameras may not show hidden damage.
choices.result: The cameras zoom in on the new mark.

choices.label: Add protective shielding
choices.result: Shield plates go up around the panels.

choices.label: Move equipment indoors
choices.result: The crew carries the loose equipment inside.

why.text: Meteoroids can strike the lunar surface and create impact craters. Moon habitats and suits must be built to withstand this.

title: The Final Samples
speaker: luna
line: The astronauts must decide which samples to collect and bring back for scientific study.
context: The crew is preparing to finish its research mission. There is limited time and space to collect rock samples.

choices.label: Collect different rocks
choices.risk: Less time remains for other research.
choices.result: Sample bags fill with rocks of every colour.

choices.label: Collect nearby rocks
choices.risk: Important samples farther away may be missed.
choices.result: The crew fills a few bags close to the base.

choices.label: Study rocks before collecting
choices.result: The crew photographs and measures each rock first.

why.text: Apollo astronauts collected more than 800 pounds of Moon rocks and soil. Scientists study these samples to learn about the Moon's history and formation.
